Green Book 2.1 theory contributes the valid-small-case workflow, recurrence discipline, and pattern-to-proof boundary to canonical simplification Knowledge.
The sequential allocation vote becomes the canonical backward-induction Problem, with the recurrence and tie assumptions exposed rather than a source-named wrapper.
The replacement-predator process becomes the canonical parity-induction Problem, with action and preference assumptions made explicit.
The mental-cube prompt is retained as a Knowledge check on arithmetic decomposition, not expanded into a low-depth public Problem.
The exponential-growth prompt is retained as a Knowledge check on backing up from a known endpoint, not expanded into a trick page.
The service-location estimate resolves to source-neutral Fermi-estimation Knowledge without publishing a dated country total.
The specialized-provider estimate resolves to source-neutral Fermi-estimation Knowledge without publishing a dated city total.
The two-resource threshold family becomes the canonical minimax recurrence Problem and receives a justified Dynamic Programming topic refinement.
The large-power digit-count family becomes the canonical strict-bounds Problem without log tables or direct expansion.
The joint-extremes comparison family becomes the canonical optimal-comparison Problem and receives a justified Algorithmic Complexity topic refinement.
The round-cover prompt is retained as a Knowledge check on structural geometry, not expanded into a one-answer public Problem.
Green Book 2.2 groups finite candidate elimination, invariant checks, and adaptive testing into the bounded Logical Deduction learning path.
The bridge family becomes the canonical state-search Problem with an independently verified optimal schedule and lower bound.
The private-information dialogue becomes a source-neutral public-announcement Problem with every candidate-set update explicit.
The two-color pairing invariant remains an executable Knowledge check rather than a low-depth standalone Problem.
The nonuniform timer remains an executable constraint-composition Knowledge check rather than a one-trick standalone Problem.
The heavy-or-light anomaly family becomes the canonical 24-hypothesis ternary decision-tree Problem.
The factorial-zero prompt is generalized to prime valuations in arbitrary bases and receives a justified Modular Arithmetic refinement.
The batched-race family becomes the canonical partial-order selection Problem and receives a justified Algorithmic Complexity refinement.
The recursive tower prompt is the existing canonical power-tower identity and merges into its complete convergence and branch-selection proof.

Reusable derivative definitions and rules, logarithmic differentiation, qualitative derivative analysis, and elementary limit theory are fused into four public Knowledge nodes with visible Interview Checks.
The canonical Problem derives the positive variable-base/variable-exponent rule, explicitly differentiates x^x on x>0, and applies the rule to the log-power case on x>1.
The canonical comparison uses the sign of the first derivative on full intervals; a second derivative is only a local check and zero is inconclusive without a sign change.
One source row contains two independent limit identities, so it resolves to two Problems; both enforce the L'Hôpital gate and the origin limit preserves its approach from below.
The canonical lighthouse Problem models s=a tan theta, derives the general related rate, and specializes one revolution per minute to 2 pi a secant-squared theta miles per minute.
The canonical Problem rationalizes sqrt(x squared plus 5x) minus x and preserves the finite limit 5/2 instead of subtracting infinities.
The canonical Problem proves exponential midpoint convexity and records equality exactly at equal endpoints.
This asks the same transcendental-power comparison as the Green item and is absorbed into one source-neutral monotonicity Problem.
The canonical recurrence starts at c0=2 with c(n+1)=2+2/cn, proves convergence of finite convergents, and only then selects 1+sqrt(3) from the fixed-point roots.
The canonical Problem differentiates the Normal CDF with sigma positive and proves the unique inflection through an actual sign change of the second derivative.
The exact harmonic, square, and logarithmic-harmonic series triple is owned by the canonical Problem and adds no separate public identity.
The x^x derivative on x>0 is absorbed into the canonical positive variable-base/variable-exponent Problem.
The canonical Problem derives the derivative of exp(cos x) from an exact difference-quotient factorization and standard limits, without Taylor series.
The reusable derivative-rule review is fused into core public Knowledge, including an Interview Check that differentiates x ln x on x>0 as ln x+1.
This is the same transcendental-power comparison already represented by the canonical monotonicity Problem.
This is the same exponential midpoint-convexity identity and is absorbed as alternate evidence rather than duplicated publicly.
This x^x derivative on x>0 is absorbed into the same canonical positive variable-base/variable-exponent Problem.
The canonical nested-radical Problem proves bounded monotone convergence before selecting the positive fixed point.
The canonical Problem first finds the positive base sqrt(2) for tower value 2, then proves the finite towers increase below 2 and reject fixed-point branch 4.
The canonical Problem proves divergence of the harmonic and logarithmic-harmonic series and convergence of the square series by elementary non-integral arguments.
Same canonical three-variable correlation-feasibility problem; this source variant contributes a geometric angle/Gram-vector derivation of the 0.28-to-1 interval rather than a new public Problem.
Canonical vector geometry Knowledge absorbs the source coordinate interpretation as a reusable definition.
Canonical vector geometry Knowledge absorbs the source dot-product definition and its interview-useful consequences.
Canonical vector geometry Knowledge absorbs Euclidean norm and distance as reusable geometry.
Canonical vector geometry Knowledge absorbs angle and orthogonality as reusable inner-product geometry.
The source correlation-as-cosine bridge enriches canonical vector geometry while linking to the existing correlation-matrix Knowledge rather than duplicating correlation theory.
Distinct matrix-invariant closure proof: row sums are preserved through the all-ones vector and entrywise nonnegativity is preserved under matrix multiplication.
Determinant identities are reusable matrix facts rather than a distinct interview problem.
Definitions, characteristic equations, multiplicities, and eigenspaces belong in canonical spectral Knowledge.
Trace and determinant as spectral invariants enrich the shared concept layer.
Diagonalization criteria and A^k in an eigenbasis are reusable concept/technique material.
A concrete 2x2 eigensystem has an independent reasoning task and supports multiple interview-ready solution routes.
The eigenvalue/eigenvector count question is best preserved as an Interview Check on multiplicity, eigenspaces, and defective matrices.
Applying A to a vector from known eigenpairs is a distinct eigenbasis-decomposition reasoning problem.
Trace cyclicity is a distinct proof task with direct index and stronger spectral interpretations.
The commutator obstruction is a distinct invariant-recognition problem using trace.

The source section mixes a correct PSD quadratic-form definition with an overbroad leading-principal-minor statement. Canonical Knowledge distinguishes PSD from the positive-definite Sylvester criterion.
Same joint-correlation feasibility family, posed as validity of a fully specified triple and naturally generalizable to an admissible interval.
The question says positive definite, while its solution correctly observes covariance matrices are only guaranteed positive semidefinite. Canonical wording uses the correct PSD claim.
Definition/properties material enriches canonical PSD/PD Knowledge and interview checks.
Existing canonical parameter-range problem.
Same covariance-PSD proof identity, extended to show the correlation matrix is PSD as well.
Distinct n-dimensional equicorrelation eigenvalue/bound problem.
Repeats the First Look parameter matrix; its additional Schur/completing-square methods enrich the existing canonical problem rather than creating another page.
Definitions and normalization identities enrich canonical covariance/correlation Knowledge rather than forming a standalone problem.
Distinct normalization/congruence-transform problem.
This source item defines reusable orthogonal-triangular factorization knowledge; it enriches canonical QR Knowledge and does not create a standalone public Problem.

This is a distinct interview reasoning task. The canonical Problem teaches direct QR on the design matrix; the source normal-equation-first presentation remains internal evidence rather than the recommended public algorithm.
LU is reusable elimination and triangular-solve knowledge here, with no independent source reasoning task that warrants a separate canonical Problem.
Cholesky belongs in the shared decomposition ontology with LU; the definition and factorization conditions enrich canonical Knowledge rather than creating a duplicate public Problem.

Generating correlated normals is an independent simulation reasoning task. The canonical Problem generalizes the two-dimensional construction to SPD Cholesky and PSD spectral or SVD covariance factors.
This item contributes reusable rectangular, rank-aware SVD knowledge and does not define a separate canonical interview Problem.

This task is the semantic anchor for the canonical matrix-square-root and Gram-factor Problem. Its entrywise square-root route is retained as an alternative method while the canonical page foregrounds reusable spectral and Cholesky structure.

This task has the same reasoning identity as the canonical matrix-square-root and factor Problem, but contributes a different matrix and useful spectral and Cholesky calculations, so it is retained as a meaningful variant inside the same public page.
Source-derived outcome, sample-space, event, union/intersection/complement, mutually-exclusive, and indicator language is preserved in probability-spaces-events and its Interview Checks.
Primary source instance of the extra-coin symmetry family; equal-n tie decomposition resolves to the source-neutral more-heads-with-one-extra-coin Problem.
Primary source instance of the tie-aware rank-symmetry family; tie mass is removed before symmetry in higher-card-by-symmetry.
Primary source instance of the displaced-passenger symmetry family; the two-special-seat state reduction resolves to drunk-passenger-last-seat.
Distinct semicircle covering Problem using event partitioning plus geometric symmetry; public targets are random-points-in-a-semicircle and its supporting event/symmetry Knowledge.
Knowledge-only equiprobable weekday-modeling self-test retained in symmetry-equiprobability-geometric-probability; it does not warrant a separate S3+ Problem.
Merged duplicate of higher-card-by-symmetry; it contributes the same tie/non-tie partition and symmetry route.
Distinct continuous geometric-probability task represented by romeo-juliet-meeting-probability and unit-square modeling Knowledge.
Merged duplicate of drunk-passenger-last-seat; wording differs but the displacement process and two-special-seat reasoning identity are the same.

This source item contributes complement-event and repeated-independence reasoning to the mixed canonical Knowledge node; it does not source or support the repository-authored Kolmogorov-axiom extension.
Merged duplicate of more-heads-with-one-extra-coin; it contributes an alternative symmetry derivation while retaining the same canonical reasoning identity.

Reusable product-rule, factorial, permutation, combination, and finite equiprobable counting material is fused into canonical counting and finite-probability Knowledge; the source definitions remain publicly testable through Interview Checks.

Distinct finite-card counting family represented by poker-hand-probabilities; the canonical page keeps one unordered five-card sample space while deriving four-of-a-kind, full-house, and exactly-two-pair counts.

Primary source instance of the random knockout-bracket placement family; fixing one top player and counting the other player’s opposite-half slots resolves to top-two-meet-in-knockout-final. The Red tournament task is merged into this same reasoning identity.

Distinct fixed-point-avoidance family represented by five-letters-all-misaddressed; the public solution derives the five-object derangement count through inclusion-exclusion instead of memorizing a source-specific answer.

Distinct collision/complement-counting family represented by birthday-collision-threshold; the canonical page derives the no-collision product and verifies that 23 is the first group size above one-half collision probability.

Merged cross-book duplicate of top-two-meet-in-knockout-final. Its mathematical identity is the same relative-placement question as the existing knockout-tournament family, so it enriches hidden evidence instead of creating a second public page.
The matching-socks task is a compact finite-state check rather than a separate S3+ reasoning family. It remains publicly visible as an Interview Check in finite-combinatorial-probability-modeling.

The two-aces with/without-replacement task is preserved as a public Interview Check that contrasts changing denominators with the equivalent unordered combination model; it does not warrant a duplicate standalone Problem.

Distinct forbidden-adjacency counting family represented by no-consecutive-heads-in-n-tosses. The canonical page derives the Fibonacci recurrence and the equivalent gap-counting identity inside a uniform 2^n sample space.

Distinct random-subset containment family represented by random-subsets-containment-probability. The canonical solution uses four elementwise membership states, forbids only membership in A without B, and obtains (3/4)^n.

Reusable conditional-probability, multiplication and chain-rule, total-probability, independence-boundary, and Bayes material is fused into canonical conditioning and Bayes/base-rate Knowledge; public Interview Checks preserve the source-derived interview tests.
Primary source instance of the two-child information-protocol family; the canonical page generalizes the conditioning event and makes the observation mechanism explicit.
Primary source instance of the latent double-headed-coin Bayes family; the canonical page generalizes the source instance to prior pi and n observed heads.
Distinct informed-reveal conditioning family represented by the source-neutral Monty Hall page with the host information policy stated explicitly.
Distinct last-occurrence conditioning family; the canonical page reduces the random removal sequence to mutually exclusive last-color orderings.
Primary source instance of the survival-conditioning roulette family; the adjacent-bullet state is represented in one canonical public Problem.
Merged duplicate of the latent double-headed-coin posterior family; its one-in-ten prior and three-head numerical case are retained as a variant inside the general canonical page.
The repeated-heads question primarily tests prior and model ambiguity. Its interview value remains visible through Bayes and conditioning Interview Checks rather than creating a second coin Problem.
Merged duplicate of the two-child information family; the canonical page handles the observation mechanism explicitly instead of preserving source-specific wording.

Named-child wording is observation-protocol dependent. The source shortcut is not copied blindly; the canonical Problem corrects the ambiguity by requiring a declared naming and information-generation mechanism before a numerical answer.

Merged duplicate of the adjacent-bullet survival-conditioning family; the survived-trigger information and one-quarter no-spin versus one-third spin comparison resolve to the shared canonical Problem.
Distinct latent-object selection-conditioning family represented by golden-face-posterior; visible-face weighting gives posterior two-thirds.

The reusable random-variable, support, CDF/PMF/PDF, and standard distribution material is fused into canonical public Knowledge. Source-derived definition and recognition checks remain visible through Interview Checks rather than creating a standalone Problem.

This row owns only the exponential waiting-time, memoryless, residual-wait, and stationary-age reasoning represented by exponential-memoryless-bus-wait. The source uses an arrival-process wrapper, but this workstream does not claim general Poisson-process or broader stochastic-process theory.
The uniform-distribution CDF task is a compact representation check preserved in the CDF/PMF/PDF and common-distributions Interview Checks; it does not require a separate canonical Problem.

The Cauchy example is preserved as a heavy-tail and moment-existence boundary check in common-probability-distributions, including the distinction between symmetry/principal value and a proper finite expectation.

Distinct distribution-pushforward reasoning family represented by density-under-random-variable-transform. The canonical page derives the transformed CDF first, then the inverse-Jacobian rule and many-to-one branch correction.

Distinct independent-sum convolution family represented by sum-of-two-uniforms-triangular-density; the canonical solution derives the piecewise integration bounds from the simultaneous support restrictions.
The classical central-limit-theorem statement is fused with the corresponding limit-theorem material into one canonical LLN/CLT Knowledge node and remains publicly testable through Interview Checks.

The exponential density, support, and parameterization are reusable distribution Knowledge; the source-derived definition remains visible through public Interview Checks instead of becoming a standalone Problem.

Distinct competing-independent-exponential family represented by exponential-race-probability; the canonical page generalizes the numerical means to the rate-share formula lambda_X/(lambda_X+lambda_Y).
The Poisson random-variable PMF and count-distribution recognition rule are fused into common-probability-distributions. This row does not claim general Poisson-process theory.

Distinct jointly-normal decorrelation and quadrant-conditioning family represented by joint-normal-quadrant-conditioning; the canonical solution makes the joint-normal requirement for zero-covariance independence explicit.

Distinct lognormal-product closure family represented by when-is-a-product-lognormal; the canonical page distinguishes independent lognormals from the more general jointly-normal-log condition and rejects marginal lognormality alone.
Weak and strong laws of large numbers are fused into the canonical limit-theorem Knowledge node, where convergence modes and public Interview Checks preserve the source-derived interview value.

The classical central limit theorem is fused with the Red CLT material into one canonical limit-theorem Knowledge node, including sqrt(n) scaling, convergence in distribution, and finite-variance boundaries.

Standard-normal MGF and moment calculations enrich the general Normal MGF/moments canonical Problem; workstream 008 intentionally left this expectation-heavy identity for the Expectation, Variance & Covariance workstream.

The section-level theory is fused into reusable expectation, conditional-expectation, and scalar variance/covariance Knowledge. Its low-complexity interview tests remain publicly visible through Interview Checks rather than thin source-specific Problems.
Ordinary size-reduction expectation recursion; no Markov-chain, martingale, or other stochastic-process machinery is required.
Scalar variance/covariance minimization defines the canonical identity; covariance-matrix PSD and spectral feasibility remain Linear Algebra ownership.
A self-consistency expectation equation creates a distinct recursive-payoff identity from the repository-authored one-step conditional-dice seed.
Random-permutation symmetry plus indicators determines the first-special position and remains distinct from pattern-count and coupon-count indicator constructions.
Geometric waiting increments give the full-collection time while indicators give the expected distinct-count formula; no process-level state machinery is required.
Fixed-marginal Bernoulli joint-probability bounds determine scalar covariance/correlation feasibility; matrix PSD remains a separate Linear Algebra identity.
The fair-die expected value is a low-complexity expectation check and remains publicly testable through the canonical expectation Knowledge Interview Checks rather than a thin standalone Problem.
Once the symmetric box game is worth starting, continuation only improves after misses; the canonical mathematical load is expected winning position and fair value.
Independent multiplicative factors give a product-expectation identity; expected wealth growth is kept distinct from log/geometric growth and Kelly optimization.
The item asks for first-principles derivation of geometric mean and variance, not merely recognition of the Geometric distribution.
Overlapping pattern indicators can be dependent, but linearity of expectation still gives the expected count; this dependence boundary is the canonical insight.
The canonical page generalizes the disk to radius R and derives the expected radius; the betting wrapper is retained only as an extension.
The general Normal MGF and second-moment calculation owns the canonical identity and absorbs the standard-normal moment variant from another source.
The standard-normal E[Phi(X)]=1/2 case is a special case and alternative symmetry/PIT perspective inside the general Normal canonical Problem.
The unit-disk expected-radius item is the R=1 instance of the general radius-R canonical Problem and contributes no separate reasoning identity.
The general Normal E[Phi(X)] identity owns the canonical Problem; the standard-normal special case from another source is retained as a variant and alternative method.
The iid Uniform maximum, minimum, and range family is represented once by uniform-sample-extremes-and-range and also absorbs the equivalent Red 3.29 source item.
Joint minimum/maximum dependence is a distinct order-statistics identity. The canonical solution uses scalar covariance algebra, while covariance-matrix PSD remains Linear Algebra ownership.
Collision relabeling reduces the random physical system to the maximum of iid Uniform remaining distances. The existing deterministic ants-crossing-line puzzle remains a separate invariance Problem.
This is the same iid Uniform maximum, minimum, and range reasoning family as Green expected-max-min, so one source-neutral canonical Problem owns both sources.
The general kth-order-statistic distribution and density form a distinct canonical identity that was intentionally left outside workstream 009.

Finite homogeneous Markov-chain theory is represented by reusable Knowledge with visible Interview Checks for matrix orientation, state structure, stationarity, hitting equations, periodicity, and positive return.
This row establishes canonical source ownership for the existing random-walk-boundary identity, enriched once with fair, biased, deterministic, and three numeric boundary cases.
The competing total-of-12 and consecutive-seven hazards form a distinct two-state streak-compression Problem with success probability 7/13.
One multipart canonical Problem owns the HHH and THH waiting times, their first-hitting race, and the exact length-three second-chooser response guarantee.
Ordered-pair recoloring from distinct initial colors is represented by backward active-lineage coalescence and the exact mean consensus time (n-1)^2.
The cube return family is a distinct canonical Problem solved both by the finite-chain mean-return identity and by Hamming-distance compression, with expected positive return 8.
The fair finite-plank walk has the same state space, absorbing boundaries, recurrence, and fair solution as random-walk-boundary, so it enriches that identity instead of creating a wrapper duplicate.
The fair walk on 0 through 1000 starting at 80 is the lower-boundary complement case of random-walk-boundary and evaluates to 92/100 = 23/25 without a second public identity.
